sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Environment questions reveal professional habits. A candidate who knows virtual environments, requirements.txt, and why secrets belong in env vars is immediately more trustworthy than one who installs everything globally and hardcodes passwords.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
**Problem → Solution chain:**

- Global installs cause conflicts → `python -m venv .venv` isolates per project
- 'Works on my machine' → `requirements.txt` pins exact versions
- Secrets in code → `.env` file + `python-dotenv` + `.gitignore`
- Modern projects → `pyproject.toml` replaces `requirements.txt` + `setup.py`

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **Create venv** — `python -m venv .venv`
- **Activate** — Mac/Linux: `source .venv/bin/activate` | Windows: `.venv\Scripts\activate`
- **Deactivate** — `deactivate`
- **Freeze** — `pip freeze > requirements.txt`
- **Install from file** — `pip install -r requirements.txt`
- **Environment variables** — `os.environ.get('KEY')`. Load from `.env` with `python-dotenv`.
- **`.gitignore`** — always include `.venv/`, `__pycache__/`, `.env`.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **'Why do you use a virtual environment?'** — project isolation; prevents dependency version conflicts between projects.
- **'What is requirements.txt for?'** — reproducible installs; `pip install -r requirements.txt` gives everyone the same versions.
- **'How do you store API keys in a Python project?'** — environment variables, never hardcoded. `.env` file with `python-dotenv`, added to `.gitignore`.
- **'What is pyproject.toml?'** — modern replacement for setup.py + requirements.txt, PEP 517/518 standard.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I always create a virtual environment for each project so dependencies are isolated. I pin them with pip freeze > requirements.txt so anyone can reproduce my environment. Secrets go in a .env file that's listed in .gitignore — never committed to git. For newer projects I use pyproject.toml with Poetry or uv."*
